tossups.text: In this organ, the bundle of His sends impulses to the Purkinje[pur-KIN-jee]fibers to control motion.In this organ, a sinus rhythm is set by the sinoatrial node, and can be interrupted in arrhythmia or by diseases like myocarditis. An E⋅K⋅G can find problems in thisorgan's four valves, two atria, and two ventricles, which send oxygenated blood out through the aorta. For ten points, name this organ responsible for pumping blood through the body.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for ventricles and csf. It plays a key role in the nervous system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this cerebrum-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The cerebrum is a key component of the Nervous system, involved in ventricles and csf.

tossups.text: A sculpture named for one of these things is bound by turquoise serpents and represents one of these things with a glyph for "movement." Four gods representing the cardinal directions created the first of these things after defeating a crocodile with mouths on its knees. The end of one of these things occurred after greedy humans were turned into monkeys and blown away in a hurricane. After one of these things is hit with a stone club, jaguars eat humanity. In one story, Nanahuatzin ("nana-WHA-tzin") becomes one of these things after Tecuciztecatl ("tec-coo-sis-tec-attle") is too scared to jump into a bonfire. Human sacrifices were made to Huitzilopochtli ("WEET-see-luh-POACH-tlee") to prevent this thing from going black. For 10 points, the Aztecs believed they lived under the fifth cycle of what celestial object, which titles a Mexica "Stone"?

This painting's leftmost figure was inspired by a cameo of Augustus riding a Capricorn owned by Domenico Grimani. A Leo Steinberg essay attempts to identify "who's who" in this painting, which serves as the backdrop for Barbara Kruger's You Invest in the Divinity of the Masterpiece. Theories about a group of twelve people in this painting include one theorizing a dangling green cloth as an umbilical cord. A bearded man in a flowing pink robe in this painting was the last figure its artist painted on custom scaffolding for a project financed by Pope Julius II. A male figure with an extra rib lounges on a green hill in this painting. For 10 points, name this Michelangelo painting on the Sistine Chapel's ceiling depicting God extending his index finger towards the first man.
acceptableAnswers: answers mentioning the Sistine Chapel ceiling with “What painting within there?”

tossups.text: In one of this man's poems, the title character interacts with seven spirits and a chamois hunter, while another poem calls the title character "the first to welcome/ foremost to defend" and laments its death. In addition to "Epitaph to a Dog" and "Manfred", this author wrote a travelogue in four cantos describing his own travels while narrated by the title character. He also wrote a mock epic about a womanizing Spaniard. For 10 points, name this poet of Childe Harold's Pilgrimage and Don Juan (pronounced Don Ju-won).

Parks in this city include one called Riverside Promenade which offers a view of a section of the city called the Bund that contains numerous buildings built by the British and French. This city's Century Park is its largest, located in Pudong, and other attractions include the Jade Buddha Temple which contains the Hall of the Kings of Heaven. A tea house is located in the center of a lake in this city located near the Yu Garden. This city is located just south of Hengsha Island and east of Lake Tai, the source of the Huangpu River which bisects this city, but more notable is this city's location on the delta of the Yangtze. For 10 points, name this Chinese port city located east of Nanjing on the East China Sea.

These phenomena ionize the outputs of supercritical and gas chromatography, allowing them to be detected. ICP is an alternative to these phenomena for performing AES. Civil engineer George Stephenson developed a containment for these phenomena but his subsequent mistreatment by the Royal Society led him to send his son to private school. Teaching labs typically avoid loops of platinum in favor of cheaper nichrome wire to introduce compounds to these phenomena. In the lab, rotating the baffles can tune these phenomena to have two distinct cones. Dissolved ions can be distinguished by adding them to these phenomena and observing the color. For 10 points, name these phenomena produced by the energetic oxidation of fuel, as through a Bunsen burner.

This compound is used in the manufacture of levothyroxine, a thyroid deficiency drug. Its two subunits are joined by an acetal oxygen bridge in the beta orientation and it is dextro-rotatory. On a scale of relative sweetness, where sucrose is 100, it ranks below maltose and galactose at 15. When undigested, it ferments in the colon and causes abdominal pain, bloating, gas, and diarrhea. Consisting of glucose and galactose this is, For 10 points, what disaccharide that comprises 4-6% of cow's milk.

Pink banana flesh appears under a yellow peel in this artist's design for the cover of the Velvet Underground's debut album. This artist used mesh to transfer ink onto a canvas to create portraits of an actress in his Marilyn Diptych, which was made using silk-screening. This artist, who worked at the Factory, created thirty-two paintings that only differ in the labels of varieties like "split pea" and "tomato." For 10 points, name this Pop artist, who painted Campbell's soup cans.

One of these areas is located at the foot of the Morro Dois Irmãos, overlooks the Rodrigo de Freitas Lagoon and is called Vidigal. The industrial development of the Meyer district created one called Jacarezinho (ja-ka-rei-ZEEN-yo). A funicular railway once served the example of Dona Marta, which is located on the edge of the Botafogo and Laranjeiras (la-ran-JEI-ras) districts, while a group of them, the Complexo do Alemão (kom-PLE-sho do a-le-MAO) is now served by a cable car. The first of them was named for a hill in Canudos populated by a certain species of spurge tree, and is now the neighborhood of Providencia. Phillip Glass composed a theme and variations based on Ravel's Bolero but utilizing the rhythms of the Samba named after the largest of these places, which surrounds the steep slopes of the Pedra da Gavea in São Conrado and is in imminent danger of landslide, the neighborhood of Rocinha (ro-SEEN-ya). For 10 points, name these slums found on the hillsides above Ipanema and Copacabana, the home of many of Rio de Janeiro's working poor.

He claimed that he is only fit to "drive chariots," the least of his "Six Arts," when asked what is his greatest strength. He advocated "the middle way" and taught the "five excellent practices" that are important to good governance. After his resignation as a minister of the Lu, he travelled to the neighboring kingdoms, and later compiled the Five Classics that preached the ideas of li, ren, and de. An advocate of the "Superior Man," for 10 points, identify this ancient Chinese philosopher whose sayings are collected in the Analects.

An artist from this country intended to "transport you to a quiet cosmos" with her immersive Infinity Mirror Rooms. That artist from this country is notable for covering objects like pumpkins with her characteristic polka dots. A performance artist from this country invited audience members to use scissors to remove pieces of her clothing in her work Cut Piece. That Fluxus art movement member from this country staged "bed-ins" against the Vietnam War with her husband. An art style from this country translated as "pictures of the floating world" includes a woodcut of a large wave. For 10 points, name this country home to Yayoi Kusama and Yoko Ono, as well as ukiyo-e artists like Hokusai.

In his Description of Greece, Pausanias describes a sacred cave in Mount Elaios in Arcadia dedicated to this deity, where an image of this deity with the head of a horse was worshipped. The Homeric Hymn to this deity describes how the deity receives a warm welcome in the home of Celeus and Metaneira, and, in return to their hospitality, tries to grant their son immortality by setting him on fire. This deity accidentally ate the shoulder of Pelops. According to legend, winter is attributed to the sorrow of this deity upon the loss of her daughter Persephone to the Underworld. For 10 points, name the Greek goddess of grain and agriculture, equivalent of the Roman deity Ceres.

In the middle of this piece's final movement, the opening theme from its first movement is re-introduced in a double fugue; this touch was likely inspired by the String Quartet No. 1 in the same key by Felix Mendelssohn, who sight-read this piece's first private performance. This piece's second movement begins as a funeral march in C minor before transitioning into a series of rapid descending scales which are doubled by the violin. This is the most innovative piece to come out of its composer's "Chamber Music Year" of 1842, as it substituted a cello for the double bass traditionally used for piece in its genre, as in Schubert's "Trout" piece. For 10 points, identify this composition for keyboard and four string players, composed by the husband of Clara Wieck.

The lamina propria is a part of a tissue covered in this substance, and antimicrobial molecules are secreted into this substance by Paneth cells. The secretion of this substance results in the diffusing out of calcium ions, which causes the repulsion of the many negative charges that cover this substance's principle constituent glycoprotein, leading to an up to 1,000-fold expansion. Guaifenesin is one drug that helps get rid of this substance and is part of a class of drugs called expectorants. H. pylori ensconces itself in this substance before secreting urease. It is secreted by goblet cells, and this substance adheres to epithelial cells and acts as a diffusion barrier and lubricant. For 10 points, name this substance that builds up in the lungs and digestive track of people with cystic fibrosis.

Irving B. Weiner's textbook on this procedure surveys the much-derided "ouija ("wee-jee") board" method of conducting it. In the 1970s, John Exner standardized the five separate scoring systems that developed after the early death of this procedure's namesake. The R-PAS guidelines for assessing results in this system accounts for traits like French subjects being more likely to identify chameleons. Unlike the MMPI, this assessment is not self-reported. This assessment consists of ten items, two of which combine gray, black and other colors; all ten items are intended to be an ambiguous stimulus to which patients respond. For 10 points, name this psychological test where patients are asked to describe images in ink blots.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on inkblot test before the end

tossups.text: this structure is essential for anterior pituitary hormones. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this hypothalamus-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The hypothalamus is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in anterior pituitary hormones.

tossups.text: A character with this first name lives in a house whose interior has not been seen for ten years, except by an old man-servant. After her father passes away, that character is given tax exemptions by her town's mayor Colonel Sartoris. Another character with this first name asks the question "Do any human beings realize life while they live it?" in a monologue. That character dies in childbirth and re-celebrates her twelfth birthday party with the help of the Stage Manager. That woman marries high school baseball phenom George Gibbs in Wilder's Our Town. For 10 points, William Faulkner wrote a short story titled "A Rose for" what character, also the first name of the author of Wuthering Heights?

In this decade, Judge Albert Oberweger ("OH-bur-vay-gur") called a defendant's story "too stupid to believe" after an assassin shot a politician because he could not identify his target in the dark. A diplomatic mission in this decade was meant to negotiate with Konrad Henlein under the auspices of Walter Runciman. In this decade, Hungarian power was increased by the Bled agreement, which was signed by the Little Entente. The self-elimination of the Austrian parliament during this decade enabled a "self-coup" by Engelbert Dollfuss. Czechoslovak leader Edvard Beneš ("BEH-nesh") was betrayed during this decade due to an agreement signed by Édouard Daladier. For 10 points, name this decade when the infamous claim of "peace for our time" was made by Neville Chamberlain in response to the Sudeten Crisis.

University of Texas professor Sanford Levinson questioned why this provision does not get more coverage in legal journals in an article titled for its "embarrassing" consequences. The 1886 Presser v. Illinois case, which said that this restriction does not apply at the state level, was challenged in April 2009 by a Ninth Circuit ruling which held that this amendment is now incorporated. The majority opinion in a recent case addressing this law noted that "a purposive qualifying phrase that contradicts the word or phrase it modifies is unknown this side of the looking glass, except, apparently, in some courses on Linguistics." An earlier Supreme Court case addressing this amendment turned on the transportation of an item from Oklahoma to Arkansas in violation of a federal registration statute and the meaning of the phrase "well-regulated militia." For 10 points, identify this subject of the DC v. Heller and U.S. v. Miller rulings, a Constitutional amendment guaranteeing the right to keep and bear arms.

parts.text: Name these numbers that are divisible by exactly two numbers: one and itself. The first few of these positive integers are 2, 3, 5, and 7.
These special primes are one less than a power of two. They are named after a French mathematician who studied them in the early 17th century.
Prime numbers are contrasted with these numbers that have at least one divisor besides 1 and itself. The only positive integer to be neither a prime number nor one of these numbers is 1.

bonuses.leadin: The first person to study these numbers was the Greek mathematician Euclid, who proved that there were an infinite number of them. For ten points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with sliding filament theory.
What is the main function of the contraction in the musculoskeletal system?
Name another component of the musculoskeletal system related to sliding filament theory.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human musculoskeletal system.

parts.text: Name these people whom Sahagun attempted to get to stop worshiping indigenous gods such as Quetzalcoatl.
Sahagun disparagingly equated this Aztec god of darkness with the pagan Jupiter. In many depictions, one of this god's feet is replaced with an obsidian mirror.
Sahagun included many of his observations on indigenous religion in this twelve-book compendium on Aztec culture, which is commonly named for a city in Italy.
acceptableAnswers: General History of the Things of New Spain
Historia General de las Cosas de Nueva España

bonuses.leadin: Bernardino de Sahagun translated Christian psalms and gospels into the language of these people, adding elements such as Mary being impregnated by a quetzal feather. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Danger Mouse first came to prominence by mashing up this rapper's Black Album with the Beatles' White Album to make The Grey Album. This rapper is married to Beyoncé.

Danger Mouse's biggest commercial success came with this hit song, made when teaming up with Cee-Lo Green in Gnarls Barkley. This song begins "I remember when, I remember I remember when I lost my mind."

Danger Mouse produced this man's sophomore album, which features the songs "Jukebox Joints" and "L$D." On "Potato Salad," a collaboration with Tyler, the Creator, this man raps, "no this ain't a purse, it's a satchel."

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about the projects of Brian Burton, better known as Danger Mouse, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this poet who lamented, "Believe me, I loved you all," in "the mother." Another poem by this author describes "two who are Mostly Good" for whom "dinner is a casual affair."

"the mother" first appeared in Brooks' collection A Street in Bronzeville, which was inspired by the South Side neighborhood of this city. A Carl Sandburg poem addressed to this Illinois city calls it "Hog Butcher of the World."

Brooks' poem "We Real Cool" is often cited as an example of this poetic technique. In this technique, a line break is inserted in the middle of a sentence without any punctuation or grammatical pause.

bonuses.leadin: This author wrote, "You were born, you had body, you died. / It is just that you never giggled or planned or cried," in a poem addressed to all of the unborn children she aborted. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this father of Humayun who founded the Mughal empire.
This fifth Mughal emperor ruled from the Red Fort, which contained the Peacock Throne. This man ordered the construction of the Taj Mahal after the death of his favorite wife, Mumtaz.
This man murdered Dara Shikoh in order to succeed Shah Jahan, whom he imprisoned. He also executed Sambhaji, the son of Shivaji, and Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Sikh guru.

bonuses.leadin: He defeated the Delhi Sultanate led by Ibrahim Lodi at the Battle of Panipat in 1526. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these hair-like projections that function in movement and are usually longer than cilia.
The internal structure of a eukaryotic flagellum consists of two central microtubules surrounded by this number of microtubule doublets.
This term refers to the entire 9 + 2 structure. It attaches to the cell at the basal body.

bonuses.leadin: The prokaryotic type of this structure rotates, while the eukaryotic type undulates. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Satellites determine position using a horizon sensor, which detects the amount of this type of radiation given off by Earth. This type of radiation is detected by thermal imaging cameras.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on “black-body radiation” by asking “In what region of the electromagnetic spectrum?”

parts.text: Satellite rotation is sensed by the ring laser type of these devices that rely on the Sagnac effect. Other examples of these orientation-sensing devices consist of a wheel suspended by three gimbals.

Satellites can stabilize using tidal forces to align an axis in a technique named after this quantity's gradient, which is a 3 by 3 tensor measured by "full tensor" devices. This quantity is measured in units of gals.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on acceleration with "acceleration induced by what force?"
prompt on field strength of "the field associated with what force?"

parts.text: Name this event that took place on the night of December 4th, 1791, in Vienna.

Mozart died roughly two months after conducting the premiere of this opera, in which Tamino plays the title instrument to help pass the trials of water and fire. An aria in this work sung by the Queen of the Night hits the F above high C.
Mozart's last completed concerto was for this single-reed woodwind instrument that, today, is tuned in B-flat.

bonuses.leadin: Franz Sussmayr took over the composition of a Requiem mass after this event, which some have theorized was triggered by Antonio Salieri.

parts.text: Name this short-form streaming platform. This company raised over a billion dollars from investors but shut down only six months after its April 2020 launch.

This founder of Quibi explained that his mobile-only platform would compete with Snapchat and Instagram, not with Netflix, in a 2019 Vanity Fair interview. This former Walt Disney Studios chairman co-founded Dreamworks.

Though Katzenberg blamed COVID-19 for Quibi's failure, this social media app crossed two billion downloads in 2020. Dances often go viral on this app, where users share short videos of themselves set to music.

bonuses.leadin: This company faced a lawsuit from Eko for purportedly stealing Turnstyle technology that allows both horizontal and vertical viewing. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Greek philosopher who also wrote the dialogues Timaeus and Crito.
The story of this legendary city which sank into the sea is related in the Platonic dialogues Timaeus and Critias.
Instructed by Plato, this founder of the peripatetics wrote the Poetics and the Nichomachean Ethics and taught at the Lyceum.

bonuses.leadin: He wrote about an attempt to define virtue in Meno and about a discussion of love at Agathon's place in Symposium. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this good produced by grinding the bodies of a scale insect that lives on prickly pear cacti. This dye gave English army coats and Catholic cardinal robes their distinctive colorations.

The red robes of this artist's portrait of Agostino Pallavicini may have been created with cochineal. This artist painted a self-portrait of himself with a sunflower and a chain awarded to him by Charles I of England.

Cochineal was used to render the fabric draped over the right shoulder of a lute-playing youth in The Musicians by this artist known for his use of tenebrism in paintings such as The Calling of St. Matthew.

bonuses.leadin: Folio 500 of the Codex Osuna depicts the production of this good, whose Nahuatl ("na-WA-tull") name is nocheztli. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this object which was eventually stolen by Cet, and used to fulfill the prophecy that the king of Leinster would have his revenge after death.

The brain ball of Mesgegra was used to kill this high king of Ulster, and noted pursuer of Deirdre, when it was used as a shot in a sling. The ball lodged there until, as later Christian legend has it, this king heard about the death of Christ and got so angry that his wound burst and he died.

The conflict over Deirdre and the murder of Noisiu by Conchobar drove this man, Conchobar's stepfather, into an allegiance with Medb. He died when Lugaidh, a warrior in the service of Ailil, Medb's husband, killed him after Ailil became jealous.

bonuses.leadin: This object was possessed by Conall, who obtained it after killing the king of Leinster and cutting off his head, which he then found impossible to lift. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this sort of cloth in which both the warp and the weft are resist dyed prior to weaving.

The resist is applied to the woven cloth in this technique which is used to make the Madiba shirt and which makes use of the canting [tsan-ting] to apply the wax which produces its characteristic pattern.
Batik is most closely associated with this country in which the Kebaya dress is worn and in which many men wear the Kain Sarung.

bonuses.leadin: This sort of cloth is used to make Patola Sari and the Oshima cloth. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this effect in which exchanging an atom for one with a different mass number causes a change in reaction rate. It is often used to determine unknown reaction mechanisms.
Replacing an atom of this element with deuterium produces a strong kinetic isotope effect, because this simple element's most abundant isotope is roughly half as massive as deuterium.
The kinetic isotope effect of this reaction mechanism is very close to 1. The Finkelstein reaction follows this mechanism.

bonuses.leadin: The secondary form of this effect happens when the substituted atom is not directly involved in a bond that's formed or broken. For 10 points each:

This American psychologist developed his namesake box to study operant conditioning in animals. He also wrote Beyond Freedom and Dignity.
Skinner also wrote this novel whose title alludes to a Henry David Thoreau work. This novel describes a utopian community run by Frazier and the Planners.

What is the main function of the diaphragm in the respiratory system?
Name another component of the respiratory system related to inspiration and expiration.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human respiratory system.

parts.text: Identify this novel by Erich Maria Remarque about Paul Baumer, who is ultimately killed by a stray bullet in the trenches fighting in World War I.
parts.answer: All Quiet on the Western Front
acceptableAnswers: All Quiet on the Western Front
The All Quiet on the Western Front

parts.text: This "terror of Klosterberg", who before the war had worked in the postal service, torments Paul and his companions in training camp. Paul and Kropp once dump a latrine bucket on his legs as a prank.
Paul eventually inherits these objects, which originally belonged to an airman before being used by Kemmerich, and, after him, Muller.

bonuses.leadin: At the 1930 premier of a film adaptation of this novel, Josef Goebbels and his Nazi cronies released itching powder and smoke bombs into the theater to show their displeasure at its pacifist message. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This heresy, which led to the Council of Nicaea, claimed that Jesus was only the highest of created beings, and not of the same substance as God
Coptic and Syrian Christians profess this aptly-named doctrine, which holds that Christ has only one nature, partly divine and partly human.
Developed in North Africa in the early 4th century, this heresy maintained that the moral character of the priest determined the effectiveness of the sacraments he performed.

bonuses.leadin: Name these Christian heresies, For 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this group of terrorists whose slogan "Za dom Spremni" means "Ready for the Fatherland."
This member of the Ustashe was installed as poglavnik by the Nazis and had an adventurous post-World War II romp through Austria, Italy, Argentina, Paraguay, and Spain.

Prince Aimone of Savoy, slightly better known as Tomislav II was the puppet ruler of this country ruled by the Ustashe during WWII. Unlike Chris Ray, he never had the balls to actually step foot in this country.
